title: Perform basic life support and/or first aid procedures in emergencies

lessons.title: Staying safe and calling for help
lessons.html:
What first aid is

First aid is the help you give a sick or hurt person before the ambulance, nurse or doctor arrives. It can save a life and stop an injury from getting worse.

Important: this lesson does not make you a first aider. To give first aid, and especially CPR, you must do hands-on training with an accredited first aid provider and practise on a training dummy.

Step 1: Danger

Look before you go near the person. Is there danger to you?

  • A tractor engine still running? Ask someone trained to switch it off.
  • A loose bull or a snake?
  • Electric wires? Do not touch the person until the power is off.
  • Chemical spill or gas? Do not walk into it.

Never become a second patient. If it is not safe, stay back and call for help.

Step 2: Response

Talk to the person loudly: Can you hear me? Tap their shoulders. See if they answer or move.

Step 3: Call for help

  • Shout for people near you.
  • Phone for an ambulance: 10177, or 112 from a cell phone. Also call your farm's emergency number and your supervisor.
  • Say clearly: what happened, how many people are hurt, and where you are, including the farm name, the road and how to find the place.
  • Send someone to the gate or main road to show the ambulance the way.
  • Ask someone to bring the first aid box.

Protect yourself from germs

Wear the gloves from the first aid box when you may touch blood or body fluids. Wash your hands afterwards.

lessons.title: Basic life support: breathing and CPR
lessons.html:
Check breathing

If the person does not answer you:

  1. Lay them on their back on firm ground.
  2. Open the airway: put one hand on the forehead and gently tilt the head back. Lift the chin with two fingers.
  3. Look, listen and feel for normal breathing for up to 10 seconds. Watch the chest go up and down.

If they are breathing normally

Put them in the recovery position: on their side, with the top leg bent to stop them rolling, and the head tilted so that vomit or blood can run out of the mouth. Stay with them. Check their breathing until help arrives. If you think the neck or back is hurt, move the person only if you must to keep the airway open or to get them out of danger.

If they are not breathing, or only gasping

Make sure someone has called the ambulance. Start CPR (cardiopulmonary resuscitation) for an adult:

  1. Kneel next to the chest.
  2. Put the heel of one hand in the centre of the chest. Put your other hand on top and link your fingers.
  3. Keep your arms straight. Push straight down hard, about 5 to 6 cm, then let the chest come all the way back up.
  4. Push fast: about 100 to 120 times a minute.
  5. If you are trained and willing, give 2 rescue breaths after every 30 pushes. If not, keep doing only chest pushes.
  6. Do not stop until help arrives and takes over, the person starts breathing normally, or you are too tired to go on. Swap with another trained person every two minutes if you can.

If a defibrillator (AED) is on the farm, ask someone to bring it, switch it on and follow its spoken instructions.

Never

  • Never give water or food to a person who is not fully awake.
  • Never leave an unconscious person lying on their back alone.

lessons.title: First aid for common farm injuries
lessons.html:
Bleeding

  1. Put on gloves.
  2. Press firmly on the wound with a clean pad or cloth.
  3. Keep pressing. If blood soaks through, put another pad on top. Do not remove the first one.
  4. Bandage the pad firmly in place.
  5. If something is stuck in the wound, do not pull it out. Press around it and get help.

Burns

  • Cool the burn under cool running water for about 20 minutes.
  • Take off rings and watches before swelling starts, unless they are stuck to the skin.
  • Cover loosely with cling wrap or a clean non-fluffy cloth.
  • Never put butter, oil, toothpaste or ice on a burn. Never pop blisters.

Broken bones

Keep the hurt part still. Support it in the position you found it. Do not try to straighten it. Get medical help.

Chemical on the skin or in the eyes

Take off wet clothes. Rinse with lots of clean running water for a long time. For eyes, keep the eye open under the water. Take the product label to the clinic.

Snake bite

  • Keep the person calm and as still as possible.
  • Call for help and get them to hospital quickly.
  • Take off rings and tight things near the bite.
  • Never cut the bite, never suck it, and never try to catch or kill the snake.

Heat stroke

If a worker is hot, confused or has stopped sweating, move them to shade, loosen clothes, cool them with water and fanning, and get help fast.

After the emergency

Tell your supervisor, write down what happened and what you did, and restock the first aid box.

Key points

  • Check for danger first; never become a second patient.
  • Call 10177 or 112, and say what happened and exactly where.
  • Not breathing normally: push hard and fast in the centre of the chest until help comes.
  • Press firmly on bleeding; cool burns with running water.
  • Hands-on training with an accredited provider is required before you give first aid.
